direction: Read this scene aloud. A quiet hilltop above a village at dusk. Pip is a young kid telling a friend a strange, sad story: hushed, earnest, unhurried, with real pauses between sentences. Grandpa is an old man: gravelly, slow, gentle, tired of explaining.
lines: The dog on the hill... hasn't moved... in nine hundred days.
Not for rain. Not for thunder. Not even for zombies.
I bring him a bone every morning. He never even looks.
He wears a red collar. But nobody in the village owns him.
He just stares... at one empty patch of grass.
And behind him... an old dirt hut. Nobody knows who built it.
I tried to make him stand. I begged. He won't budge.
Leave him be, kid. Only one voice gets him up.
Whose? Nobody's come up here in years.
So every night now... I sit with him. Nobody should wait alone.

direction: Read aloud as a young man, warm and casual, a little distracted, greeting his dog happily for a moment before he has to go again:
lines: Okay. Sit, boy. I'll be right back.
